      "source": [
        "# Forecast example\n",
        "\n",
        "This notebook introduces the basic workflow using the `py_online_forecast` package.\n",
        "\n",
        "It covers:\n",
        "- Data handling with the `fc` accessor,\n",
        "- feature engineering using transformations,\n",
        "- minimal forecasting example using `WLS`,\n",
        "- online forecasting using `ForecastModel`,\n",
        "- multi-horizon forecasting using `ForecastEnsemble`,\n",
        "- transforms and sources,\n",
        "- hyperparameter optimization."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 45,
      "id": "b4d8418d",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [],
      "source": [
        "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
        "import numpy as np\n",
        "import pandas as pd\n",
        "from scipy.optimize import minimize\n",
        "\n",
        "from py_online_forecast import *\n",
        "from py_online_forecast.datasets import sample_data\n",
        "from py_online_forecast.forecast_tools import ForecastFormat, Subset\n"
      ]
    },

      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "66c1c005",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "## Data\n",
        "\n",
        "This example uses simulated sample data from `py_online_forecast.datasets.sample_data`.\n",
        "\n",
        "The sample data is a pandas DataFrame following the \"forecast-matrix\" format. This requires that\n",
        "- the columns are a two level MultiIndex of feature names and forecast horizons,\n",
        "- the index is monotonically increasing and evenly spaced.\n",
        "\n",
        "The feature names can be freely chosen, whilst the forecast horizons should be a non-negative integer. A forecast horizon of zero corresponds to \"now\" and may be used for observed values.\n",
        "\n",
        "### The `fc` accessor\n",
        "\n",
        "To support the forecast format, a custom `pandas` accessor with name `fc` can be used. The `fc` accessor provides convenience methods for working with forecast-matrix data. We begin by subsetting the data based on the horizons,"
      ]
    },

      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "55459666",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "## Sources & Transformations\n",
        "The `py_online_forecast` package is built around `Source` and `Transformation` objects. A `Source` instance is a placeholder for data, and a `Transformation` instance is a source that has methods for processing data. Most transformations require other sources as inputs and are used to define data transformations for feature engineering. When data arrives, they should be matched to sources (using a `dict`), after which all transformations may be resolved. "
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 39,
      "id": "c42dd71a",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [
        {
          "data": {
            "text/plain": [
              "array([10, 20, 30])"
            ]
          },
          "execution_count": 39,
          "metadata": {},
          "output_type": "execute_result"
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "raw_data = Source(\"Raw data\")\n",
        "\n",
        "transformed_data = raw_data*10\n",
        "\n",
        "raw_data_value = np.array([1, 2, 3])\n",
        "\n",
        "transformed_data({raw_data: raw_data_value})"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "670d8ce7",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "If no source is specified for a piece of data, it will be matched to `DEFAULT_SOURCE`. With this, we can simplify the above to"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 41,
      "id": "d505a3a3",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [
        {
          "data": {
            "text/plain": [
              "array([10, 20, 30])"
            ]
          },
          "execution_count": 41,
          "metadata": {},
          "output_type": "execute_result"
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "transformed_data = DEFAULT_SOURCE*10\n",
        "transformed_data(raw_data_value)"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "f7b2b393",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "For basic usage, it is convenient to build our data pipeline from this source. For example, we may want to make 1-step forecasts of the `energy` variable using an intercept, the observed temperature `Taobs` and the 1-horizon forecasts `Ta`."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 6,
      "id": "e6009ae2",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [],
      "source": [
        "energy = DEFAULT_SOURCE[[\"energy\"]]\n",
        "const = One()\n",
        "taobs = DEFAULT_SOURCE[[\"Taobs\"]]\n",
        "ta = Subset(DEFAULT_SOURCE, \"Ta\", horizons=(1,))"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "99c305d0",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "In the above, `energy`, `const`, `taobs` and `ta` are all transformations. Except for `const`, they are all explicitly defined from a source (`DEFAULT_SOURCE`). Behind the scenes `One` also uses an input source, but tacitly assumes it to be the `DEFAULT_SOURCE`. The `Subset` transformation assumes input values to be of forecast-matrix type, and selects variables and horizons.\n",
        "\n",
        "To see the output of the transformations, we can call them on the data, e.g."
      ]

        "Some transformations are not memory-less, i.e. they require some state or old data to continue where they left of. An example of this is the `LowPass` filter, which requires the previous value of the input time series. In an online setting, data cannot be processed in batch, and handling of such \"memory\" states is important.       ]

        "This information can then be passed to new calls of the transformation in order to resume computation from the old state. To make this more convenient, we may instead use the `track_state` flag, making the transformation handle the memory state and automatically use it in future calls, e.g.,"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 13,
      "id": "dec3dbec",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [

            "text/plain": [
              "{Subset(['Ta'], horizons=(1,)): [False, False, True, False, False],\n",
              " ToArray: None,\n",
              " LowPass: array([15.40295399])}"
            ]
          },
          "execution_count": 13,
          "metadata": {},
          "output_type": "execute_result"
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "lp_Ta(data, track_state = True)\n",
        "lp_Ta.recursion_pars"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "4d41dff9",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "> **Note:** If a transformation is called again **without** `track_state=True`, any stored state will not be used, nor will it be overwritten."
      ]

      ]

      "source": [
        "## Basic prediction\n",
        "The goal in this section is to forecast the `energy` variable using the ambient temperature observation and forecast transformations defined previously. To do so, we first form a design matrix for a weighted-least-squares type problem,"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 15,
      "id": "6b99f78e",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [],
      "source": [
        "X = DesignMatrix(const, lp_Taobs, lp_Ta)"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "df5d5321",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "We can then define a prediction model using the `WLS` transformation,"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 16,
      "id": "a6af1f87",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [],
      "source": [
        "pred = WLS(X, energy, horizon=1)"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "b81c14e5",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "Calling the prediction on the data fits the model and returns predictions. With `track_state=True`, recursive state such as fitted WLS parameters is stored and can be inspected afterwards."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 17,
      "id": "c2bc7c60",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [
        {
          "data": {
            "text/plain": [
              "array([[53.97516386],\n",
              "       [-0.85765934],\n",
              "       [ 0.67845426]])"
            ]
          },
          "execution_count": 17,
          "metadata": {},
          "output_type": "execute_result"
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "result = pred(data, track_state=True)\n",
        "pred.predictor\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "a4635999",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "For convenient use with forecast-matrix data, the output can be wrapped in `ForecastFormat`.\n"
      ]
    },

      "source": [
        "As a simple check, compare the fitted coefficients with a direct NumPy least-squares estimate.\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 19,
      "id": "b70c20f0",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [
        {
          "name": "stdout",
          "output_type": "stream",
          "text": [
            "Model parameters from OLS model: [[53.81844016]\n",
            " [-0.82042603]\n",
            " [ 0.65485707]]\n",
            "Model parameters from numpy lstsq: [[53.97516386]\n",
            " [-0.85765934]\n",
            " [ 0.67845426]]\n"
          ]

        "beta_ols = pred.predictor\n",
        "\n",
        "pred.reset_state()\n",
        "X_data = pred.X(data)\n",
        "X_train_data = X_data[:-1]\n",
        "Y_data = pred.Y(data)\n",
        "\n",
        "beta_np = np.linalg.lstsq(X_train_data, Y_data.to_numpy()[1:], rcond=None)[0]\n",
        "\n",
        "print(f\"Model parameters from OLS model: {beta_ols}\")\n",
        "print(f\"Model parameters from numpy lstsq: {beta_np}\")\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "140f7db3",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "## Online forecasting with recursive ridge regression\n",
        "For online forecasting, the standard WLS approach is sub-optimal. We will instead use the purpose built `RRR` transformation via. the wrapper class `ForecastModel`. The `RRR` transformation functions similarly to the `WLS` transformation, but uses a recursive ridge regression estimator. The `ForecastModel` provides convenience features for forecast-matrix data. We can define a model as,"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 20,
      "id": "1928dd2a",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [],
      "source": [
        "X = (const, lp_Taobs, lp_Ta)\n",
        "model = ForecastModel(X, energy, 1, track_memory=True, init_K=0.00001)\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "f590840f",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "Then the `fit` method resets the state (if any) and applies the transformation."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 21,
      "id": "e5762717",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [
        {
          "data": {
            "image/png": "",
            "text/plain": [
              "<Figure size 1000x400 with 1 Axes>"
            ]
          },
          "metadata": {},
          "output_type": "display_data"
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "result = model.fit(data, mem=1)\n",
        "\n",
        "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4))\n",
        "data.plot(y=\"energy\", ax=ax)\n",
        "result[\"mean\"].shift(1).plot(ax=ax)\n",
        "plt.legend([\"Observations\", \"Forecast\"])\n",
        "plt.show()\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "4c6cc99f",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "### Multivariate target\n",
        "\n",
        "The recursive ridge workflow also supports multivariate targets.\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 22,
      "id": "c3eecf79",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [
        {
          "data": {
            "image/png": "",
            "text/plain": [
              "<Figure size 1000x400 with 1 Axes>"
            ]
          },
          "metadata": {},
          "output_type": "display_data"
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "target = DEFAULT_SOURCE[[\"energy\", \"Taobs\"]]\n",
        "model_multi = ForecastModel(X, target, horizon=1, track_memory=True, init_K=0.00001)\n",
        "result_multi = model_multi.fit(data, mem=1)\n",
        "\n",
        "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4))\n",
        "data.plot(y=\"energy\", ax=ax)\n",
        "data.plot(y=\"Taobs\", ax=ax)\n",
        "result_multi[\"mean\"].shift(1).plot(ax=ax)\n",
        "plt.legend([\"Energy obs\", \"Taobs\", \"Energy forecast\", \"Taobs forecast\"])\n",
        "plt.show()\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "e65f5190",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "### 3.4 Simulate online updates\n",
        "\n",
        "To emulate an online setting, data is passed to the model one observation at a time.\n",
        "\n",
        "Inputs are assumed to have observations along the first axis. For a single observation, this means using a one-row DataFrame such as `data.iloc[[i]]`.\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 23,
      "id": "ee30558e",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [
        {
          "name": "stdout",
          "output_type": "stream",
          "text": [
            "True\n"
          ]
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "subsets = [data.iloc[[i]] for i in range(len(data))]\n",
        "\n",
        "model.reset_state()\n",
        "predictions = []\n",
        "\n",
        "for s in subsets:\n",
        "    p = model.update(s, mem=1)[\"mean\"]\n",
        "    predictions.append(p)\n",
        "\n",
        "predictions = pd.concat(predictions)\n",
        "\n",
        "print(np.allclose(result[\"mean\"].to_numpy()[1:], predictions.to_numpy()[1:]))\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 24,
      "id": "9cece78a",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [
        {
          "data": {
            "text/plain": [
              "{'mean': Variable                energy\n",
              " Horizon                      1\n",
              " 2130-01-01 00:00:00  48.268914\n",
              " 2130-01-01 01:00:00  49.295261\n",
              " 2130-01-01 02:00:00  49.162442\n",
              " 2130-01-01 03:00:00  48.522786\n",
              " 2130-01-01 04:00:00  48.629899\n",
              " ...                        ...\n",
              " 2130-01-09 03:00:00  49.251509\n",
              " 2130-01-09 04:00:00  48.748764\n",
              " 2130-01-09 05:00:00  47.893458\n",
              " 2130-01-09 06:00:00  47.248101\n",
              " 2130-01-09 07:00:00  47.234056\n",
              " \n",
              " [200 rows x 1 columns],\n",
              " 'cov': Variable            (energy, energy)\n",
              " Horizon                            1\n",
              " 2130-01-01 00:00:00        29.754629\n",
              " 2130-01-01 01:00:00        29.601694\n",
              " 2130-01-01 02:00:00        29.617114\n",
              " 2130-01-01 03:00:00        29.705725\n",
              " 2130-01-01 04:00:00        29.691394\n",
              " ...                              ...\n",
              " 2130-01-09 03:00:00        29.619501\n",
              " 2130-01-09 04:00:00        29.676239\n",
              " 2130-01-09 05:00:00        29.818046\n",
              " 2130-01-09 06:00:00        29.953284\n",
              " 2130-01-09 07:00:00        29.954957\n",
              " \n",
              " [200 rows x 1 columns]}"
            ]
          },
          "execution_count": 24,
          "metadata": {},
          "output_type": "execute_result"
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "model.update(data, update_predictor=False)\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "b5f9ed7f",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "## Multi-horizon forecasting\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "e7c9df6f",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "A simple approach for making multi-horizon predictions is to make a new model for each. Here we create a second model for the 2-hour-ahead forecast.\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 25,
      "id": "3d2acf43",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [],
      "source": [
        "ta2 = Subset(DEFAULT_SOURCE, \"Ta\", horizons=(2,))\n",
        "lp_Ta2 = LowPass(ta2, alpha=0.8)\n",
        "X2 = (const, lp_Taobs, lp_Ta2)\n",
        "\n",
        "model_2h = ForecastModel(X2, energy, horizon=2, track_memory=True, init_K=0.00001)\n",
        "\n",
        "ref_1h = model.fit(data, mem=1)\n",
        "ref_2h = model_2h.fit(data, mem=1)\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "675032b7",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "### Model ensembles\n",
        "In many cases, such two models may share many basic input features, and we may benefit from evaluating them in a single pass without recomputing known values. The `Combine` transformation evaluates all inputs and returns a `dict` with the results."
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 26,
      "id": "2f1f356d",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [
        {
          "data": {
            "text/plain": [
              "(Variable                energy\n",
              " Horizon                      1\n",
              " 2130-01-01 00:00:00        NaN\n",
              " 2130-01-01 01:00:00  52.477670\n",
              " 2130-01-01 02:00:00  54.352502\n",
              " 2130-01-01 03:00:00  50.405863\n",
              " 2130-01-01 04:00:00  56.399926,\n",
              " Variable                energy\n",
              " Horizon                      2\n",
              " 2130-01-01 00:00:00        NaN\n",
              " 2130-01-01 01:00:00        NaN\n",
              " 2130-01-01 02:00:00  53.309106\n",
              " 2130-01-01 03:00:00  43.747420\n",
              " 2130-01-01 04:00:00  19.704705)"
            ]
          },
          "execution_count": 26,
          "metadata": {},
          "output_type": "execute_result"
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "models = Combine(model, model_2h)\n",
        "result = models(data, mem=1)\n",
        "\n",
        "result_model_1h = result[model]\n",
        "result_model_2h = result[model_2h]\n",
        "\n",
        "result_model_1h[\"mean\"].head(), result_model_2h[\"mean\"].head()\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "aabb6219",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "### The `ForecastEnsemble`\n",
        "\n",
        "`ForecastEnsemble` creates multiple models and splits forecast-matrix data by horizon. The `input_horizons` argument (also supported by `ForecastModel`) determines which of the input features to use based on the horizon. If `auto` is selected, the model will use horizons $(0,h)$ where $h$ is the forecast horizons of the given model.\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 29,
      "id": "1b30c1ac",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [],
      "source": [
        "ta_all = DEFAULT_SOURCE[[\"Ta\"]]\n",
        "lp_Ta_all = LowPass(ta_all, alpha=0.8)\n",
        "Xall = (const, lp_Taobs, lp_Ta_all)\n",
        "\n",
        "horizon_models = ForecastEnsemble(\n",
        "    Xall,\n",
        "    energy,\n",
        "    horizons=(1, 2),\n",
        "    input_horizons=\"auto\",\n",
        "    track_memory=True,\n",
        "    init_K=0.00001,\n",
        ")\n",
        "\n",
        "horizon_result = horizon_models.fit(data, mem=1)\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "dbe5a704",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "Just as before, we can also make updates in an online manner,"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 30,
      "id": "b0ab40ed",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [
        {
          "name": "stdout",
          "output_type": "stream",
          "text": [
            "True\n"
          ]
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "horizon_models.reset_state()\n",
        "predictions = []\n",
        "\n",
        "for s in subsets:\n",
        "    p = horizon_models.update(s, mem=1)[\"mean\"]\n",
        "    predictions.append(p)\n",
        "\n",
        "predictions = pd.concat(predictions, axis=0)\n",
        "\n",
        "print(np.allclose(horizon_result[\"mean\"].to_numpy()[2:], predictions.to_numpy()[2:]))\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "8b682ab3",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "## Hyperparameter optimization\n",
        "Model hyperparameters, including transform parameters and predictor settings, can be optimized by scoring the fitted model. To enable this, prediction transformations (such as `RRR` and `ForecastModel`) may expose a \"score mode\". For these models, setting score mode will add an extra evaluation step in the transformation, which includes a \"score\" in the output.\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "f9764df0",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "Say for instance a slow trend is added to the data.\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 42,
      "id": "8f1dda29",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [],
      "source": [
        "trend_data = data.copy()\n",
        "trend_data[(\"energy\", 0)] += 0.1 * np.arange(len(trend_data))"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "4b42396d",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "The optimal low-pass filter parameter may depend on the data, and we thus estimate it in an outer loop,"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 43,
      "id": "cacfbf9b",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [
        {
          "name": "stdout",
          "output_type": "stream",
          "text": [
            "       message: Optimization terminated successfully.\n",
            "       success: True\n",
            "        status: 0\n",
            "           fun: 5.700395088827669\n",
            "             x: [ 3.377e-01  9.324e-01]\n",
            "           nit: 63\n",
            "          nfev: 120\n",
            " final_simplex: (array([[ 3.377e-01,  9.324e-01],\n",
            "                       [ 3.378e-01,  9.324e-01],\n",
            "                       [ 3.377e-01,  9.324e-01]]), array([ 5.700e+00,  5.700e+00,  5.700e+00]))\n"
          ]
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "\n",
        "\n",
        "model.set_score_mode()\n",
        "\n",
        "def obj(x):\n",
        "    alpha, mem = x\n",
        "    lp_Taobs.alpha = alpha\n",
        "    lp_Ta.alpha = alpha\n",
        "    return model.fit(trend_data, mem=mem)[\"score\"]\n",
        "\n",
        "res = minimize(obj, x0=[0.5, 0.5], bounds=[(0, 1), (0, 1)], method=\"Nelder-Mead\")\n",
        "print(res)\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "7fbac24e",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "The `ForecastEnsemble` enables a similar approach,"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "execution_count": 44,
      "id": "a04dc90d",
      "metadata": {},
      "outputs": [
        {
          "name": "stdout",
          "output_type": "stream",
          "text": [
            "       message: Optimization terminated successfully.\n",
            "       success: True\n",
            "        status: 0\n",
            "           fun: 6.1434452045205035\n",
            "             x: [ 4.374e-01  9.250e-01]\n",
            "           nit: 61\n",
            "          nfev: 116\n",
            " final_simplex: (array([[ 4.374e-01,  9.250e-01],\n",
            "                       [ 4.375e-01,  9.250e-01],\n",
            "                       [ 4.375e-01,  9.250e-01]]), array([ 6.143e+00,  6.143e+00,  6.143e+00]))\n"
          ]
        }
      ],
      "source": [
        "horizon_models.set_score_mode()\n",
        "\n",
        "def obj_horizon(x):\n",
        "    alpha, mem = x\n",
        "    lp_Taobs.alpha = alpha\n",
        "    lp_Ta_all.alpha = alpha\n",
        "    result = horizon_models.fit(trend_data, mem=mem)\n",
        "    return np.mean(list(result[\"score\"].values()))\n",
        "\n",
        "res_horizon = minimize(\n",
        "    obj_horizon,\n",
        "    x0=[0.5, 0.5],\n",
        "    bounds=[(0, 1), (0, 1)],\n",
        "    method=\"Nelder-Mead\",\n",
        ")\n",
        "print(res_horizon)\n"
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "id": "16fa83e4",
      "metadata": {},
      "source": [
        "## Custom transforms and predictors\n",
        "..."
      ]
